title: Where the Same Story Lives in Different Hills

features.name: the-landmark-that-multiplies
features.desc-on-touch: a stone marker stands here, but when you walk toward it, you find seven identical markers at different distances—each telling the same story but in a different dialect, era, or emotional register. approach one and another becomes visible. the tale reorganizes itself by location.

features.name: the-game-played-in-all-directions
features.desc-on-touch: a field has been marked out for a game—lines and circles in chalk—but the game's rules change depending on which ridge you approach from. played on one hill it's a strategy game; on another, a children's rhyme; on a third, a harvest ritual. the same board, rewritten.

features.name: the-story-distributed-across-stations
features.desc-on-touch: radio receivers, one per hill, each broadcasting the same story on different frequencies. you can hear them interfering with each other—the narrative fragments, recombines, becomes a chorus. the story only makes sense when heard from everywhere at once, from nowhere in particular.

features.name: the-tale-rewritten-by-terrain
features.desc-on-touch: pages of a story pinned to posts along a walking route—each page contains the same chapter, but rewritten by the person who walked to that post. the story has become a map; the map has become a story; readers walk the narrative and narrate the walk.

features.name: the-hollow-where-all-versions-sing
features.desc-on-touch: a depression in the land where the story echoes back from all surrounding hills simultaneously—a choir of versions, each slightly different in timing. when all versions arrive at once, they create a single unified resonance that belongs to none of them individually.

inscription: a tale filed in seven paddocks, each telling a different version, each version truer than the last
